source: William Lilly Christian Astrology 1647 original Wellcome b30338724
source_window: Original PDF400 below divider through original PDF402 bottom; next Chapter LII heading PDF403 is boundary only
authoring_method: Visually inspected original 1647 PDF400/401/402/403. Normalized editor phrasing; original print and margin glyphs authoritative; not independently blinded or empirically validated.

rows.source_anchor_editorial_normalization: CHAP. LI. Of Battle, Warre, or other Contentions.
rows.source_statement: Chapter LI begins below the printed horizontal divider following Chapter L.

rows.source_anchor_editorial_normalization: whether he shall overcome his Adversary or not
rows.source_statement: The opening question is whether the querent will overcome an adversary.

rows.source_anchor_editorial_normalization: give to the Querent the Lord of the ascendant the Moon and the Planet from whom she is separated
rows.source_statement: Assign the ascendant lord, Moon, and planet Moon separated from to the querent in the opening contest method.
preconditions: In the opening adversary question, assign to querent: ascendant lord; Moon; and the planet FROM which Moon separated.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: These are source-defined roles, not verified outcomes.

rows.source_anchor_editorial_normalization: unto the Defendant, the seventh and his Lord, and the Planet to whom the Moon applyeth
rows.source_statement: Assign seventh house, seventh lord, and planet to which the Moon applies to the defendant; sentence crosses printed pages 366–367.
preconditions: Assign to defendant: seventh house; seventh lord; and planet TO which Moon applies. Printed clause physically crosses original pages400→401.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Do not replace the planet Moon applies TO with the planet from which she separated.

rows.source_anchor_editorial_normalization: behold whose Significator is in Angles and best and with better Planets
rows.source_statement: Compare the appointed significators' angular positions, dignity and association with more favorable planets before the author's judgment.
preconditions: Consider the respective significators' angular status, strength and companion planets before the outcome comparison.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: How to aggregate competing testimonies is not explicitly quantified.

rows.source_anchor_editorial_normalization: If evill Planets be in the Ascendant, and Fortunes in the seventh, the Adversary shall overcome
rows.source_statement: Unfortunate planets in the first with fortunate planets in the seventh are said to favor the opponent.
preconditions: Unfortunate planet(s) in ASC AND fortunate planet(s) in seventh; outcome author attributes to adversary.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Historical judgment, not an observed outcome.

rows.source_anchor_editorial_normalization: & e contra
rows.source_statement: The author adds a converse to the prior first-versus-seventh benefic/malefic example, attributing advantage to the querent under the reversed pattern.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The converse is abbreviated; preserve its connection to the immediately preceding condition.

rows.source_anchor_editorial_normalization: The Lord of the seventh in the Ascendant, betokens victory to the Querent
rows.source_statement: Seventh lord placed in the ascendant is said to favor the querent.
preconditions: Seventh house lord in ascendant; victory is ascribed to querent.

rows.source_anchor_editorial_normalization: & e contra
rows.source_statement: A second abbreviated converse follows the seventh-lord-in-first statement; the exact inverse placement/consequence should not be treated as fully enumerated.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Do not invent a precise equation from 'e contra' alone.

rows.source_anchor_editorial_normalization: Whether one shall returne safe from Warre, or any dangerous Voyage
rows.source_statement: New heading on return from war or dangerous voyage; distinct from defeating an adversary.

rows.source_anchor_editorial_normalization: Lord of the Ascendant be strong, and with a good Planet, and well disposed
rows.source_statement: Ascendant lord strong, favorably associated, and well disposed is called a testimony of secure return.
preconditions: Ascendant lord strong AND with a good planet AND well disposed; safe return authorial claim.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The conjunction of strength, benefic association and good disposition is explicit.

rows.source_anchor_editorial_normalization: & e contra
rows.source_statement: A converse is given to the previous security testimony.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Inverse is source shorthand and not a mechanically enumerated conjunction.

rows.source_anchor_editorial_normalization: seventh and the Lord thereof, and if they be Fortunate (although the first be not so)
rows.source_statement: Fortunate seventh house and seventh lord, despite an unfavorable first, are said to imply eventual return accompanied by significant losses and impediments.
preconditions: Seventh house and its lord fortunate even when first is not; source claims eventual return WITH losses/obstacles.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Preserve safe return AND adverse losses together, not a blanket positive.

rows.source_anchor_editorial_normalization: & e contra
rows.source_statement: The author adds a converse to the seventh-fortunate despite first-weak condition.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The exact altered outcome and conjunction are not spelled out.

rows.source_anchor_editorial_normalization: Behold also the Moon how she is disposed; for her application with the good is Fortunate
rows.source_statement: Evaluate Moon's condition; application to a benefic is described as favorable.
preconditions: Moon applies to a good planet; Moon's own condition must also be observed.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Moon's aspect/application must not be silently replaced by her house placement.

rows.source_anchor_editorial_normalization: & e contra
rows.source_statement: An unfavorable converse is added to the Moon-application testimony.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: No exact degree/orb threshold provided.

rows.source_anchor_editorial_normalization: Evill Planets also in the eight, are no small Signification of feare, and terrour, or death
rows.source_statement: Malefics in the eighth are presented as an indication of fear, terror or death.
preconditions: Malefic planet(s) in eighth; adverse alternatives fear/terror/death.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The alternatives are not all unavoidable outcomes; no factual injury-risk prediction is validated.

rows.source_anchor_editorial_normalization: Saturn signifies ruines or bruises, Mars or the Dragon's Tail wounds by Weapons
rows.source_statement: Differentiate source symbolism: Saturn—ruins/bruises; Mars or the South Node—weapon wounds.
preconditions: Saturn category=bruises/ruins; Mars OR printed node-like glyph category=weapon wounds.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Planetary glyphs in print control; do not transform into medical advice.

rows.source_anchor_editorial_normalization: If one shall returne safe from Warre
rows.source_statement: Second safe-return subsection heading; do not merge with previous dangerous-voyage paragraph.

rows.source_anchor_editorial_normalization: Lord of the Ascendant be with good or good himself, or a good Planet in the Ascendant
rows.source_statement: Ascendant lord associated with a benefic, itself fortunate, OR a benefic in first are alternative indicators of safe return.
preconditions: First lord with a good planet OR itself good OR benefic planet in first; any one is printed as a safe-return testimony.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Original 'or' conditions are alternatives, not three jointly required conditions.

rows.source_anchor_editorial_normalization: if the Sun be with the Lord of the Ascendant ... he may not goe; because the Sun burns him
rows.source_statement: Sun conjunct the ascendant lord anywhere in the question is given as a warning against departure, attributed to combustion.
preconditions: Sun with ascendant lord at any part of the chart; source advises no departure and attributes this to burning.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Contrasts with blanket Sun-as-benefic interpretation; no modern safety claim.

rows.source_anchor_editorial_normalization: Lord of the seventh be with a good Planet, and the Lord of the Ascendant with an evill
rows.source_statement: Seventh lord with benefic AND first lord with malefic is said to yield impediment but not death.
preconditions: Seventh lord with benefic AND ascendant lord with malefic; source says impediment yet no death.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Both sides' relations are conjunctive; the outcome contains an explicit no-death exception.

rows.source_anchor_editorial_normalization: evill Planet be with the Lord of the first, and a good one in the first
rows.source_statement: Malefic with first lord AND benefic in first is said to yield loss, wounding, yet not death.
preconditions: Malefic with first lord AND benefic in first; source predicts loss/wounds but explicitly excludes death.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Losses, injury and explicit no-death clause must all be kept.

rows.source_anchor_editorial_normalization: If Saturn be in the first, or with the Lord of the first, let him not goe
rows.source_statement: Saturn in first OR with first lord is given as advice against going, linked to loss from someone encountered.
preconditions: Saturn in first OR with first lord; the author advises against travel.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: The alternative Saturn placements are not a joint requirement.

rows.source_anchor_editorial_normalization: if an ill Planet be with the Lord of the first, and Saturn in the Ascendant ... wounded with Wood or Stone
rows.source_statement: Malefic with first lord AND Saturn in ascendant or with its lord is said to produce wounding by wood or stone; 'or Stone' continues p368.
preconditions: Malefic with first lord AND Saturn in first OR Saturn with first lord (grouping requires care); original wood/stone consequence crosses PDF401→402.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Keep original conjunctive/alternative syntax; this is historical not clinical evidence.

rows.source_anchor_editorial_normalization: If Mars or the Dragon's Tail be in the Ascendant, or with the Lord thereof, or evill Planets in the first
rows.source_statement: Mars or South Node in first/with first lord OR malefics first/with lord is said to cause a grievous wound near death.
preconditions: Mars OR South Node in first or with first lord; OR malefics in first or with lord. Clause contains alternative groups, not necessarily all required.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Original grammar contains ORs; do not assume every listed placement is required.

rows.source_anchor_editorial_normalization: if an evill Planet be in the eight, it is to be feared, death will ensue
rows.source_statement: Malefic in eighth is a separate historical death-warning testimony.
preconditions: Malefic planet in eighth; author raises death as feared outcome.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Not empirically predictive of actual risk of death.

rows.source_anchor_editorial_normalization: if the Sun be with the Lord of the seventh, or in the eight, it is ill to goe
rows.source_statement: Sun with seventh lord OR in eighth is offered as warning against the journey; source adds elliptical 'and so of the tenth and seventh'.
preconditions: Sun with seventh lord OR Sun in eighth; terminal 'so of tenth and seventh' remains ambiguous.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Do not construct precise additional pairs or aspects from the unfinished/elliptical tail.

rows.source_anchor_editorial_normalization: What will ensue of the Warre
rows.source_statement: New heading introducing two-sided war outcomes, distinct from return-from-war safety.

rows.source_anchor_editorial_normalization: the first House signifieth the Querent, the seventh his Adversary
rows.source_statement: For this war-outcome subsection, identify the first house/first lord with querent and seventh/seventh lord with opponent.
preconditions: First house/lord denote querent; seventh house/lord denote opposing party in this subsection.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Contextual assignments are local to the printed method.

rows.source_anchor_editorial_normalization: good Planets be in the first, and malevolent in the seventh, and Lord of the Ascendant good
rows.source_statement: Benefics in first AND malefics in seventh AND strong first lord/weak seventh lord are said to favor querent.
preconditions: Good planets in first AND evil in seventh AND first lord well conditioned AND seventh lord ill.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Do not simplify to benefic-first placement alone.

rows.source_anchor_editorial_normalization: Infortune be with the Lord of the Ascendant, and an evill Planet in the Ascendant, and the Lord of the seventh good
rows.source_statement: A separately specified converse with malefic associated with first lord, malefic in first, and well-conditioned seventh lord/benefic in seventh is said to defeat the querent, possibly capture or death.
preconditions: Malefic with ascendant lord AND malefic in first AND seventh lord well conditioned AND benefic in seventh.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Original includes multiple AND terms; this is a claimed historical result not a medical or legal forecast.

rows.source_anchor_editorial_normalization: both the Lords of the Ascendant and seventh be in the Ascendant ... good Planets casting benevolent aspects to the cuspe of the second
rows.source_statement: Both first/seventh lords in first, plus benefics aspecting the second-house CUSP, are claimed to favor the querent and financial gain.
preconditions: First AND seventh lords in ascendant; benefics casting benevolent aspects to SECOND-HOUSE CUSP, on the ascendant lord's behalf.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Second cusp is the object, not necessarily second ruler. The 'on behalf of first lord' condition remains attached.

rows.source_anchor_editorial_normalization: he shall have victory ... or they will endeavour to be reconciled
rows.source_statement: Under the preceding compound first-house/second-cusp conditions, the author presents victory OR reconciliation as outcomes; do not treat them as simultaneously guaranteed.
preconditions: Inherits preceding both-lords-ASC and benefic-to-second-cusp conditions; outcomes victory OR potential reconciliation.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Same condition as previous record, not an independent new chart test.

rows.source_anchor_editorial_normalization: both the Lords, viz. of the first and seventh, be in the Ascendant, and good Planets be on the part of the Ascendant, and evil on the part of the seventh
rows.source_statement: Both house lords in first AND benefics on querent side/malefics on seventh side are said to yield loss for both, with querent better in the end.
preconditions: Both first and seventh lords in ASC; benefics on ascendant side and malefics on seventh side; both suffer, querent better at end.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Do not omit both-sides-loss qualification.

rows.source_anchor_editorial_normalization: If the Lord of the seventh be in the Ascendant ... it shewes the Fortune of the Actors
rows.source_statement: Seventh lord in first is again linked to the fortune of the actors in this war-outcome context.
preconditions: Seventh lord in ASC in war-outcome subsection; 'fortune of Actors' referent unresolved.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Author's referent 'Actors' is not independently defined beyond this paragraph.

rows.source_anchor_editorial_normalization: the contrary noteth the contrary
rows.source_statement: The prior seventh-lord-in-first clause is followed by the distinct printed phrase 'the contrary noteth the contrary'; detailed inverse placements are not enumerated.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Exact reverse configuration and opponent result not specified; do not make it a precise executable rule.

rows.source_anchor_editorial_normalization: Any Planet in the 10, 11, 12, 1, 2, 3 is conceived a friend to the Querent
rows.source_statement: Printed marginal grouping assigns planets in houses 10,11,12,1,2,3 to the querent's side.
preconditions: Printed margin classes houses 10/11/12/1/2/3 as querent's party.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: This is an original margin note, not a modern astrological generalization.

rows.source_anchor_editorial_normalization: all Planets in the 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4 are reputed for the Quesited
rows.source_statement: Printed marginal grouping assigns planets in houses 9,8,7,6,5,4 to the quesited/opponent's side.
preconditions: Printed margin classes houses 9/8/7/6/5/4 as quesited's party.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Retain complementarity and original printed margin status.

rows.source_anchor_editorial_normalization: Lord of the Ascendant be in the eight, or with the Lord of the eight, or the Lord of the eight in the Ascendant
rows.source_statement: First lord in eighth OR with eighth lord OR eighth lord in first is said to signify death of querent.
preconditions: First lord in eighth OR first lord conjoined with eighth lord OR eighth lord in first.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Multiple alternatives; unsupported as a real mortality predictor.

rows.source_anchor_editorial_normalization: Lord of the seventh be in the second, or with the Lord thereof, or the Lord of the second in the seventh
rows.source_statement: Seventh lord in second OR with second lord OR second lord in seventh/with seventh lord is said to signify death of adversary.
preconditions: Seventh lord in second OR with second lord OR second lord in seventh OR with seventh lord.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Do not leave off the last 'with the Lord of the seventh' alternative.

rows.source_anchor_editorial_normalization: CHAP. LII. Who shall doe best in a suit of Law.
rows.source_statement: Chapter LII begins at the top of original PDF403/printed369; no Chapter LII body is included as a Chapter LI source rule.
exceptions_and_uncertainty: Navigation-only boundary, not an accepted substantive result.
